rows.description: Teenage fans of rival stars trade insults online and feel united against the other side. Being part of a war is thrilling, and it can slide from banter into cruelty.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager learns that an admired person has done something wrong and works through disappointment. They keep what was good in the work without excusing the behaviour.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult defends a star or leader whatever they do, since criticising them feels like criticising oneself. Parasocial closeness feels real while the figure does not know they exist.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult finds friends, creative outlets and comfort in a fan community during a lonely time. Healthy fandom gives connection without demanding hatred of others.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: An adult sees fans abusing critics or a rival's family online. They recognise how group identity can permit cruelty and choose not to join.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A mature fan enjoys their team or artist deeply while admitting faults and treating rival fans as people. Loyalty and honesty can live together.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Helping together at school or in a colony [Actor]
rows.description: A child joins a clean-up or charity drive with friends and feels proud that together they made a difference. Small collective acts teach that ordinary people can change things.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: First cause a teenager cares about [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager joins a campaign about the environment, school rules or a local issue. They feel passion and belonging, and can also feel certain that everyone who disagrees is wrong.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult joins a peaceful protest out of conviction and feels fear, pride and solidarity at once. They weigh risk to safety, studies and family against the cause.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: fear, pride, calm, trust

rows.description: A young adult finds parents anxious about their involvement in protest or politics. The parents' fear is about safety and reputation, and calm conversations about risk help more than defiance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: hostility, fear, anxiety, calm
